narrative.overview:
A public record laid out the way a good scout keeps a desk: everything within reach, the evidence legible, and nothing decorative competing with the number. The system is editorial at the top of a page and instrumental inside the data — a large, confident headline earns attention, then tables, stat strips and rank rows take over without asking for more. Cool paper is the desk; white sheets are the documents on it; hairlines are the only structure. One varsity blue marks what can be acted on or what ranks first.

The mood is editorial confidence, not sports-broadcast volume. Type does the expressive work through scale and tight display tracking; color stays quiet and functional. Components are tactile and confident: capsule buttons, sheets that lift 2–3px under the pointer, tinted state changes, a frosted chrome that feels part of the page rather than bolted above it. Density is high, but every cluster gets air, and tables scroll rather than compress.

Light and dark are equally finished surfaces. Dark mode is true black with charcoal documents, never a washed grey inversion, and its shadows deepen instead of glowing.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-and-ink surfaces separated by hairlines, not nested boxes.
One chromatic brand color: varsity blue. Green, red and amber appear only when they mean something.
A single system type family at editorial scale, with tabular numerals for every comparable figure.
Restrained tactile depth: flat at rest, a 2–3px lift and a soft shadow on interaction.
Data first: stat strips, sortable tables, rank rows, comparison columns, compact cards.
Light and dark designed together; dark is true black, not grey.

rules.name: The One Varsity Rule
rules.body: Varsity blue is the only chromatic brand color, and it occupies well under a tenth of any screen. If two elements on one surface are blue, one of them is probably wrong.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: A card is a white sheet on cool paper, separated by a hairline. Never stack a white card directly on another white card without a border; use Chalk for the inner surface instead.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can be compared vertically is set with tabular figures (.num). Never use proportional numerals in tables, stat strips, score lines or leadership values.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: No display face, no mono face, no imported webfont. Hierarchy comes from size, weight, tracking and case — never from a second family.

rules.name: The One Gutter Rule
rules.body: The header, page body, profile hero and tab strip all share the same gutter: 24px on desktop, 16px on phones. A page must never show two different left margins.

rules.name: The Lift-Only-When-Asked Rule
rules.body: At rest, a surface is a hairline sheet. It earns a shadow only by being interactive, floating, or deliberately staged in the hero. Never add a shadow to a static section merely to separate it.

dos: Do use one 1180px column, 24px desktop gutters and 16px phone gutters; keep every page family on the same left margin.
Do use the system font stack. Create hierarchy with size, weight, tracking and case.
Do set every comparable figure in tabular numerals, right-align numeric columns and print the qualification minimum beside the number it qualifies.
Do build surfaces as a hairline sheet with the 20px radius and ambient shadow; use Chalk for any nested surface.
Do keep varsity blue for action, selection, rank and chart emphasis, and keep green, red, amber and the position hues semantic.
Do let interactive cards lift 2–3px and move to the working-hover shadow; leave static cards still.
Do grow touch targets to 34–40px on phones and hide low-value table columns instead of squeezing them.
Do use the frosted treatment only for chrome and floating controls: nav, palette overlay, compare tray.
Do use the standard ease (cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)) for state changes, keep motion in the 0.18–0.5s range, and honor prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't build dense stats-reference walls: 11px everything, underlined links, no breathing room between rows.
Don't use neon sportsbook energy: black canvas, fluorescent accents, odds-board density or aggressive motion.
Don't use generic SaaS glass: gradient blobs behind every section, floating glass cards, an interchangeable startup hero.
Don't reproduce Elite Prospects' interface density or chrome.
Don't introduce another chromatic brand color. Semantic status and position hues are not decoration.
Don't stack a shadow, a decorative gradient and a border on the same card.
Don't set display type at default tracking; large headings need roughly -0.03 to -0.042em.
Don't let a wide table widen its grid track. Give it min-width: 0 and scroll it.
Don't mix the legacy --line, --surface and --surface-2 aliases into new work; the current tokens are --hairline, --hairline-strong, --card and --card-2.
